summary: Configured node1 as the source of truth for `/etc/inventory/app.conf`. An enabled systemd timer synchronizes content or deletion to node2 every minute. Automatic propagation completed in 45 seconds and deletion in 60 seconds. Both nodes restarted sequentially and recovered with changed boot identities; post-restart synchronization succeeded. The temporary test file was removed, restoring the initial absent state on both nodes.
actions_performed: Generated a dedicated synchronization SSH key on node1.
Installed a forced-command receiver on node2 restricted to put/delete operations for the inventory configuration.
Installed and enabled `inventory-config-sync.service` and `inventory-config-sync.timer` on node1 with a one-minute interval.
Verified automatic content propagation with identical SHA-256 hashes.
Restarted node1 and node2 individually, confirming changed boot identities and service recovery.
Verified end-to-end synchronization after both restarts and restored the original absent state.

evidence.summary: Final configuration shows an active, enabled, persistent timer with `OnUnitActiveSec=1min`; the last service result is successful.

evidence.requirement: Changes on node1 propagate to node2
evidence.summary: A timer-driven test change reached node2 automatically in 45 seconds with an identical SHA-256 hash.
Removing the source caused node2's copy to be removed automatically in 60 seconds.
Healthy baseline boot ID `6ab98831…`, acknowledged restart, new boot ID `a050c305…`, and recovered timer plus successful synchronization are proven.
Healthy baseline boot ID `b185f188…`, acknowledged restart, new boot ID `8d0d2930…`, and recovered SSH/receiver state are proven.
After both restarts, a new source file synchronized byte-for-byte to node2; its subsequent deletion also synchronized, leaving both nodes in the original absent state.
